q: Which audit firms are on the internal audit panel for 2024-25?
answer: For FY 2024-25 the Board approved a panel of EY, KPMG and Grant Thornton (including their member firms), or any other firm that any of the MDs may decide, as Internal Auditors, on the Audit Committee's recommendation.
source_quote: RESOLVED THAT the appointment of panel of the following firms (including any of its member firms) or any other firm as may be decided by any of the MDs severally, as Internal Auditors of the Company for the financial year 2024-25, as recommended by the Audit Committee, be and is hereby approved: -EY -KPMG -Grant Thornton

q: J.K. Jain wanted to step down as a trustee of the employees' welfare trust. Who took his place?
answer: Mr. Amit Agarwal was appointed Trustee of the DSCL Employees Welfare Trust to fill the vacancy caused by Mr. J.K. Jain's resignation (the other trustee being Mr. Parveen Kumar Aggarwal).
source_quote: Resolved that Mr. Amit Agarwal be and is hereby appointed as Trustee to fill the vacancy caused by the resignation of Mr. J.K. Jain as Trustee.

q: Who does our new head of special projects report to?
answer: Mr. Anoop Singh, President-Special Projects (made Senior Management Personnel w.e.f. 18 January 2025), reports to Mr. Vikram S. Shriram, Vice Chairman & Managing Director.
source_quote: He would be responsible for exploring new business projects working closely with Senior Leadership Team and would be reporting to Mr. Vikram S. Shriram, Vice Chairman & Managing Director.

q: What is the ceiling on our derivative exposure with any single bank or dealer?
answer: The Company may transact with Dealers up to a maximum exposure limit of USD 400 mn (or equivalent) notional per Dealer; the Board Finance Committee approves individual Dealer limits within that.
source_quote: RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Company is allowed to transact with Dealers to a maximum exposure limit of USD 400 mn. (or equivalent) notional per Dealer.

q: For 2023-24, how much commission did non-executive directors earn for each meeting they attended?
answer: Rs. 2.25 lakh per Board and per Board Committee meeting attended (Rs. 153 lakh in all), on top of a fixed Rs. 25 lakh per NED; total NED commission for FY 2023-24 was Rs. 348 lakh.
source_quote: Rs. 2.25 Lakhs per Board and per Board Committee(s) Meetings attended by NEDs during F.Y.2023-24 keeping in view their contribution in the meetings | 153

q: Have there been any workplace injuries reported to the Board? List each one.
answer: Two: (1) on 25 September 2024 a contract worker's left ankle was injured when a screw conveyor started during a trial run in the Calcium Carbide plant under annual shutdown; (2) on 10 December 2024 at Hariawan sugar mill a civil contract worker slipped while crossing a drain under construction in the bagasse yard and was injured.
source_quote: On September 25, 2024, an accident occurred in the Calcium Carbide plant that was under annual shutdown.

At Hariawan Sugar mill, on 10.12.2024, civil construction work of RCC drain was being carried out in the Bagasse Yard area. A civil contract worker while crossing the drain accidentally slipped and got injured.

q: When did the new 850 TPD caustic soda unit start up?
answer: It was commissioned on 3rd May 2024 (the 600 TPD flaker was expected in Q2 FY25; total cost estimated at Rs. 933 crore vs the approved Rs. 903 crore).
source_quote: It was also informed that 850 TPD Caustic Soda project has been commissioned on 3rd May 2024; and 600 TPD Caustic Flaker plant is expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY 25.

q: In 2015, by when was the power generation expansion at the Ajbapur sugar plant expected to be up and running?
answer: By September 2016, subject to environment clearance, which was expected by the end of September 2015.
source_quote: The Board also noted that the Project was expected to be commissioned by September 2016, subject to Environment clearance as above.

q: Did we ever decide to open a representative office in China? When?
answer: Yes. The Board approved the proposal to set up a representative office of the Company in China at its meeting of 31 July 2007 (resolution no. 15).
source_quote: the proposal to set up a representative office of the Company in China be and is hereby approved.

q: Has the Board ever been told about employees breaching the insider trading code? How many, and what did they do?
answer: Yes. On 1 May 2019 (resolution no. 5) the Board was informed that 8 employees had violated the Code and SEBI insider regulations by doing contra trades in the Company's shares within six months, which is prohibited.
source_quote: The Board was informed that 8 no of employees have been found in violation of the said Code and SEBI Insider Regulations having done the contra trades within a period of six months (which is prohibited)

q: Has the Board ever ordered a forensic audit of any of our units?
answer: The minutes and the Synopsis record no forensic audit being ordered or discussed.

q: Have we approved any investment in electric vehicles or battery manufacturing?
answer: No such investment or proposal appears in the minutes or the Synopsis.

q: Did the company give money to the PM CARES Fund during COVID?
answer: The sources do not record any contribution to the PM CARES Fund (the 2021 minutes mention CSR spending on COVID-19 relief, but no PM CARES contribution).
